quote: it's also got a little over an acre of land. So I was thinking about using, like, a corner of the property
stewart_read: Customer is enthusiastic and proactive about solar placement — this is a highly engaged lead, just misaligned on mount type, not a low-interest customer.
coaching_implication: Rep should have leaned into this enthusiasm to keep the customer warm for a future call rather than letting the tone drift toward a full walk-away.

quote: Unfortunately, we we actually don't anymore. We've kinda moved away from ground mounts
stewart_read: Rep gives a detailed cost/trenching rationale for why Ion doesn't do ground mounts — closer-tier justification a setter shouldn't need to build out in this much technical detail.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive: rep is filling dead air with justification instead of quickly pivoting to qualify for a future roof-based sale.
coaching_implication: A shorter line ('We focus on roof installs currently') would avoid inviting the debate that follows at 02:09.

quote: I I I really don't wanna put it on the roof.
stewart_read: This is a home/roof-type objection blocking the roof-mount alternative; rep concedes immediately without asking why (new roof, aesthetics, shading) or probing whether the objection is solvable.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic: rep may have judged pushing further was pointless since the customer has a hard land-use plan, but no evidence rep tested that assumption.
coaching_implication: Ask 'what's driving that — is it look, or something about the roof itself?' before conceding; probing may have surfaced the outbuilding plan sooner.

quote: It seems like, you know, I could get so much more I could get way more panels on a quarter of an acre than on the top of a little house.
stewart_read: Second touch on the ground-mount preference — customer is actively challenging Ion's policy, a live objection, and rep responds with mechanics (bill-offset sizing) instead of reframing toward what Ion CAN offer for his situation.
coaching_implication: Rep could reframe: 'Totally fair — but since we size to your usage not max output, a roof system built to your bill could still cut your bill significantly. Want me to grab your bill and see?' instead of explaining panel economics abstractly.

quote: I'm gonna refinance and put up another building on the property that's gonna have a wood shop and three parking spots
stewart_read: Customer describes a large future outbuilding — a strong candidate for a future roof-mount or even a new cross-sell surface — but rep doesn't flag or capture this as a routing/reminder note beyond a vague future callback.
coaching_implication: Rep should have captured specifics (timeline, building size, planned power needs) to hand off for a scheduled recontact rather than a generic 'take you out for now.'

quote: I'll make a note and take you out for now. But then, yeah, when we can look out to calling you in a few months
stewart_read: Call ends without a locked callback date, no bill or utility captured, and no verbal handshake confirming next steps — a fully soft exit.
coaching_implication: Rep should lock a specific month/date for recontact ('Let's plan for a call back in [month] once your outbuilding plans firm up — does that work?') instead of a vague 'few months.'
